[Management API](admin-api.html)

What an issued Verifiable Credential carries.

Every answer is checked against the model shown here before it is sent, and no answer carries a member its model does not list. A member shown as *any JSON* is one whose shape belongs to somebody else, and says whose. `.{key}` is a key that is data, and `[]` an element of a list.

## A refusal

Unless an operation below says otherwise, any status it does not list answers this:

|---|---|---|---|
| `error` | string |  |  |
| `error_description` | string |  |  |
| `errors` | list |  |  |

| `message` | string |  |  |

| `why` | string |  |  |

## GET /admin-api/credential-claims

`getCredentialClaims`

**Which claims an issued Verifiable Credential carries**

The catalogue, what is selected from it, and a preview of what one person's credential would carry if it were issued now.

The catalogue is of LDAP ATTRIBUTE TYPES and not of claim names, because this service has a directory and a claim whose value nothing else can see is half a demonstration: the value of a claim is the value on that person's entry under ou=users.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/vc` on the admin console.

The reply also carries `protocolEndpoints`: every endpoint of this family in the realm the call arrived in, as `{ name, methods, url }` (plus `route` for an HTTP endpoint, `transport` for a socket, and `registered: false` for a route the router no longer has).

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `user` | query | string |  | Whose credential to preview. Defaults to a person the directory holds from startup, so the preview shows real values on a fresh process. |

## POST /admin-api/credential-claims/select

`selectCredentialClaims`

**Set the whole credential claim set**

Replaces the selection, and then SWEEPS THE DIRECTORY: every person under ou=users gains the selected attributes they are missing, invented from their username — deterministically, so one username is one invented person across restarts. An attribute already there is never overwritten, so an operator's `ldapmodify` and the seeded people's own names survive.

The sweep is the point rather than a side effect: without it, selecting `title` would change every future credential and change nothing an LDAP client could see, and the two halves of this service would stop describing the same people. The reply's `sweep` says what it did, including when there was no directory to do it to.

The issuer METADATA is built from this same selection, so what is advertised cannot drift from what is minted.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/vc#vc-tab-claims` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attributes` | list | yes | LDAP attribute type names, from the catalogue. |
| `attributes[]` | string |  |  |

**200**: What is selected now, what changed, and what the sweep did.

|---|---|---|---|

| `added[]` | string |  |  |
